avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
styles.flux_notes: FLUX produces convincing impressionist textures; faces may smear; fine.

styles.name: Post-Impressionism
styles.name_th: โพสต์อิมเพรสชันนิสม์
styles.historical_background: Post-impressionism names changes to Impressionism from about 1886; the term was coined by Roger Fry for his 1910 London exhibition Manet and the Post-Impressionists, and usually covers Cézanne, Seurat, Gauguin and Van Gogh, each pushing structure, scientific colour, imaginative subjects or emotional brushwork (Tate, 'Post-impressionism').
styles.visual_characteristics: Bold contours or structured planes, intense colour, expressive directional brushwork.
styles.line_characteristics: Visible contours (dark or coloured), rhythmic strokes.
styles.color_characteristics: Intense, emotional or symbolic colour; complementary contrasts.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Bright, often flattened; colour carries light.
styles.texture_characteristics: Thick directional strokes or flat areas.
styles.composition_characteristics: Tilted perspectives, flattened space, strong patterns.
styles.time_optic_fit: Fine as an occasional art post; avoid imitating Van Gogh's swirl clichés.
styles.prompt_template: Post-impressionist painting of {subject} in {setting}, bold contours, intense complementary colour, directional rhythmic brushstrokes, simplified solid forms, {palette}, {lighting}, {composition}, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Post-impressionist painting of a small optical shop counter with a vase of marigolds and a pair of green frames, bold contours, intense complementary colour, directional rhythmic brushstrokes, simplified solid forms, orange and deep green palette, bright afternoon light, tilted tabletop perspective, no text.
avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
styles.flux_notes: FLUX defaults to Van Gogh swirls when asked for post-impressionism; describe 'structured planes' or 'flat colour areas' instead.

styles.name: Pointillism (Divisionism)
styles.name_th: พอยต์ทิลลิสม์
styles.historical_background: Neo-impressionism, led by Seurat and Signac, used divisionism, often called pointillism (a label Signac rejected): tiny adjacent dabs of colour that mix in the viewer's eye; it drew on Chevreul's colour theory published in Paris in 1839 (Tate, 'Neo-impressionism').
styles.visual_characteristics: Image made entirely of small dots of pure colour; luminous, still, orderly.
styles.line_characteristics: No lines; edges from dot density.
styles.color_characteristics: Pure hues placed side by side; complementary dots in shadows.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Bright even daylight, shimmering optical glow.
styles.texture_characteristics: Uniform dot texture.
styles.composition_characteristics: Static, balanced, horizontal bands.
styles.time_optic_fit: Nice tie-in to vision science (colour mixing in the eye) for an optical shop; low detail.
common_mistakes: dots on only part of image
styles.prompt_template: Pointillist painting of {subject} in {setting}, made entirely of small dots of pure unmixed colour that mix optically, complementary dots in shadows, simplified still forms, {palette}, {lighting}, {composition}, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Pointillist painting of a park on a Sunday afternoon with a family picnicking, made entirely of small dots of pure unmixed colour that mix optically, complementary dots in shadows, simplified still forms, greens, oranges and blues, bright even daylight, horizontal bands of lawn, river and sky, no text.
avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
styles.flux_notes: Untested here; FLUX often mixes dots with regular painting; add 'entirely of dots'.

styles.name: Expressionism
styles.name_th: เอ็กซ์เพรสชันนิสม์
styles.historical_background: Expressionism emerged among German artists in the early twentieth century, with groups Die Brücke and Der Blaue Reiter; it was persecuted after 1933 and denounced in the 1937 Degenerate Art exhibition; it uses vivid non-naturalistic colour, distorted forms, loose brushwork and thick paint to convey inner feeling (Tate, 'Expressionism').
styles.visual_characteristics: Distorted angular figures, clashing colour, raw brushwork, anxious atmosphere.
styles.line_characteristics: Thick jagged outlines, rough strokes.
styles.color_characteristics: Non-naturalistic, acidic greens, reds, blues.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Unnatural, emotional; light not physically consistent.
styles.texture_characteristics: Thick, rough paint or woodcut-like marks.
styles.composition_characteristics: Tilted perspectives, crowded or claustrophobic space.
styles.time_optic_fit: Useful for showing eye strain/headache feelings in stories; too unsettling for promos.
styles.prompt_template: Expressionist painting of {subject} in {setting}, distorted angular forms, vivid non-naturalistic colour, thick rough brushwork, tilted perspective, {palette}, {lighting}, {composition}, emotional intensity, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Expressionist painting of an office worker rubbing tired eyes in front of a glowing monitor late at night, distorted angular forms, vivid non-naturalistic acid green and red, thick rough brushwork, tilted perspective of the room, harsh screen glow on the face, figure crowded into the lower corner, emotional intensity, no text.
avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
styles.flux_notes: Untested here.

styles.name: Fauvism
styles.name_th: โฟวิสม์
styles.historical_background: Fauvism flourished c.1905–1910; critic Louis Vauxcelles coined the name after seeing work by Matisse and Derain at the 1905 Salon d'Automne in Paris; it used unnatural vivid colour often straight from the tube, loose dabs and flat zones of hue rather than modelled space (Tate, 'Fauvism').
styles.visual_characteristics: Wild unnatural colour, flat colour zones, loose energetic strokes, simplified forms.
styles.line_characteristics: Loose coloured contours.
styles.color_characteristics: Pure tube colour, complementary clashes (green faces, red trees).
styles.lighting_characteristics: Colour replaces light and shadow.
styles.texture_characteristics: Loose dabs, bare canvas patches.
styles.composition_characteristics: Flattened space, decorative arrangement.
styles.time_optic_fit: Good for colourful frame collections and festive posts; clashes with the calm brand palette, so use sparingly.
styles.prompt_template: Fauvist painting of {subject} in {setting}, wild unnatural pure colours in flat zones, loose energetic strokes, simplified forms, coloured contours, {palette}, {composition}, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Fauvist painting of a woman in round red glasses on a balcony overlooking a harbour, wild unnatural pure colours in flat zones (green shadows on her face, pink sea), loose energetic strokes, simplified forms, coloured contours, vermilion, emerald and ultramarine, flattened decorative space with the window as frame, no text.
avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
styles.flux_notes: FLUX gets vivid colour; may keep realistic shading; ask 'flat zones, no realistic shading'.

styles.name: Cubism
styles.name_th: คิวบิสม์
styles.historical_background: Cubism emerged c.1907–08 in Paris, founded by Picasso and Braque; subjects split into planes showing several viewpoints at once, flattening the canvas; analytical cubism (1908–12) used muted tones, synthetic cubism (c.1912–14) brighter colours, simpler shapes and collage (Tate, 'Cubism').
styles.visual_characteristics: Fragmented planes, multiple viewpoints, overlapping facets, flattened space.
styles.line_characteristics: Straight edges, grid-like facet lines.
styles.shape_language: Geometric facets, cylinders, cones, overlapping planes.
styles.color_characteristics: Analytical: browns/greys/ochres; synthetic: brighter flat colours and textures.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Shading per facet, inconsistent by design.
styles.texture_characteristics: Faceted brushwork; collage paper in synthetic phase.
styles.composition_characteristics: Central dense cluster fading to edges; grid scaffolding.
use_cases: 'see from every angle' concept for frames
styles.time_optic_fit: Clever tie-in: 'one frame, every angle' concept; keep real photos of angles as collage pieces for accuracy.
common_mistakes: faces with eyes in wrong places as cheap joke
styles.prompt_template: Cubist painting of {subject} in {setting}, fragmented into overlapping geometric planes showing several viewpoints at once, flattened space, {palette}, faceted shading, {composition}, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Synthetic cubist still life of a pair of glasses, a coffee cup and a newspaper-textured paper scrap on a café table, fragmented into overlapping geometric planes showing several viewpoints at once, flattened space, deep green, ochre and cream palette with paper textures, faceted shading, dense central cluster fading to edges, no readable text.
avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
styles.flux_notes: FLUX produces generic 'cubist' faces easily; still lifes give better control. Untested in project.

styles.name: Art Nouveau
styles.name_th: อาร์ตนูโว
styles.historical_background: Art nouveau emerged in the 1890s, reached wide audiences after the 1900 Paris Exposition Universelle and flourished until the First World War; it is defined by sinuous lines and flowing organic plant-based shapes, seen in Guimard's Paris Métro entrances and Mackintosh's Glasgow work (Tate, 'Art nouveau').
styles.visual_characteristics: Whiplash curves, plant and flower ornaments, decorative borders, flowing hair.
styles.line_characteristics: Elegant flowing contour lines of varied weight.
styles.color_characteristics: Muted naturals (sage, ochre, dusty rose) with gold.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Flat decorative, little shadow.
styles.texture_characteristics: Lithographic flat colour, fine linework.
styles.composition_characteristics: Central figure framed by ornamental arches/borders.
styles.time_optic_fit: Good for decorative borders around frame photos and elegant women's frames; plant ornaments pair well with brand greens.
styles.prompt_template: Art nouveau decorative illustration of {subject} in {setting}, sinuous whiplash lines, flowing plant and flower ornament, ornamental arch frame, flat lithographic colour, {palette}, {composition}, no text, no lettering.
styles.prompt_example: Art nouveau decorative frame border of curling jasmine vines and lotus stems around an empty oval centre for a glasses photo, sinuous whiplash lines, flowing plant ornament, flat lithographic colour, sage green, deep green, peach and muted gold palette, symmetrical vertical composition, no text, no lettering.
avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
styles.flux_notes: FLUX adds fake lettering in nouveau 'posters'; frame as 'border' not 'poster'.

styles.name: Art Deco
styles.name_th: อาร์ตเดโค
styles.historical_background: Art deco flourished in the 1920s–30s in furniture, decorative arts and architecture; it took its name from the 1925 Paris International Exhibition of Modern Decorative and Industrial Arts, and, unlike art nouveau, was shaped by cubism and drew on Egyptian and Central American art and modern transport design (Tate, 'Art deco').
styles.visual_characteristics: Geometric symmetry, sunbursts, stepped forms, chevrons, metallic accents.
styles.line_characteristics: Crisp straight lines, fine parallel pinstripes, arcs.
styles.color_characteristics: Black, gold, cream, emerald/jade, deep teal.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Glossy highlights on metal and lacquer; dramatic uplight.
styles.texture_characteristics: Lacquer, brass, marble, glass.
styles.composition_characteristics: Symmetrical, vertical, radiating sunbursts.
styles.time_optic_fit: Strong fit for premium/gold frames — black, gold and deep green echo brand phthalo green.
styles.prompt_template: Art deco design of {subject} in {setting}, geometric symmetry, sunburst and stepped motifs, fine gold pinstripes, lacquer and brass surfaces, {palette}, {lighting}, {composition}, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Art deco background panel for a luxury eyewear display, geometric symmetry with a stepped sunburst behind an empty central plinth, fine gold pinstripes on deep phthalo green lacquer, black and cream accents, soft uplight with glossy highlights, symmetrical vertical composition, no text.
avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
styles.flux_notes: FLUX makes strong deco patterns; check symmetry and remove stray letters.

styles.name: Bauhaus Modernist
styles.name_th: โมเดิร์นนิสม์บาวเฮาส์
styles.historical_background: The Bauhaus was founded by Walter Gropius in Weimar in 1919, moved to Dessau in 1925–26 and Berlin in 1932, and was closed by the Nazis in 1933; it gave architecture, design and applied arts equal weight with fine art, with teachers including Kandinsky, Klee, Moholy-Nagy and Albers (Tate, 'Bauhaus').
styles.visual_characteristics: Primary shapes (circle, square, triangle), grids, asymmetrical layouts, sans-serif-ready space.
styles.line_characteristics: Straight bars and rules, geometric arcs.
styles.color_characteristics: Primary red, yellow, blue plus black/white/grey.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Flat, no illusionistic light.
styles.texture_characteristics: Smooth flat print, occasional paper grain.
styles.composition_characteristics: Asymmetrical grid balance, diagonals, functional hierarchy.
styles.time_optic_fit: Very usable as a layout logic for HTML carousels (grids, geometric frame shapes = round/square/cat-eye); swap primaries for brand tokens.
styles.prompt_template: Bauhaus-inspired modernist composition of {subject}, built from circles, squares, triangles and bars on an asymmetric grid, flat {palette} colours, {composition}, generous clean space, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Bauhaus-inspired modernist composition representing three frame shapes — a circle, a square and a soft triangle — built from flat geometric shapes and bars on an asymmetric grid, deep green, peach, snow white and raisin black, diagonal balance across the canvas, generous clean space, no text.
avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
styles.flux_notes: Better built directly in HTML/SVG than generated; FLUX adds noise and text.

styles.name: Constructivism
styles.name_th: คอนสตรักติวิสม์
styles.historical_background: Constructivism emerged in Russia around 1915, founded by Tatlin and Rodchenko; a manifesto appeared in Lef in 1923 and the movement was suppressed in Russia during the 1920s, with Gabo and Pevsner carrying its ideas west; it held art should reflect the modern industrial world (Tate, 'Constructivism').
styles.visual_characteristics: Diagonal bold geometry, photomontage, red/black on cream, dynamic angles.
styles.line_characteristics: Thick bars, rules, arrows.
styles.shape_language: Rectangles, circles, wedges in dynamic tension.
styles.color_characteristics: Red, black, cream, occasional grey.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Flat graphic; high-contrast photo fragments.
styles.texture_characteristics: Printed paper, halftone photo.
styles.composition_characteristics: Strong diagonals, low-angle photos, radial thrust.
styles.time_optic_fit: Usable for urgent sale/announcement graphics with brand colours; historical political associations, so avoid propaganda imagery.
common_mistakes: aggressive tone unsuitable for a friendly shop
styles.prompt_template: Constructivist-inspired graphic composition of {subject}, bold diagonal geometric bars and circles, high-contrast photomontage element, flat {palette} colours, {composition}, printed paper texture, no text, no political symbols.
styles.prompt_example: Constructivist-inspired graphic composition of a pair of glasses shot from a dramatic low angle, bold diagonal bars and a large circle, high-contrast black and white photo element, flat deep green, peach and black on cream, strong diagonal thrust from lower left to upper right, printed paper texture, no text, no political symbols.
avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
styles.flux_notes: Untested; expect fake Cyrillic text — negate.

styles.name: Surrealism
styles.name_th: เซอร์เรียลิสม์
styles.historical_background: Apollinaire coined 'surrealism' in a 1917 play preface, and André Breton's Surrealist Manifesto (1924) defined it as 'pure psychic automatism'; the Paris-based group drew on dreams and the unconscious through automatic drawing and writing (Tate, 'Surrealism').
styles.visual_characteristics: Dream logic, impossible juxtapositions, realistic rendering of irrational scenes, long shadows.
styles.line_characteristics: Precise rendering (veristic) or automatic loose line.
styles.shape_language: Familiar objects in unfamiliar scale or context.
styles.color_characteristics: Clear, often desert/sky tones; or dark dream palettes.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Low raking light, long shadows, eerie stillness.
styles.texture_characteristics: Smooth precise paint.
styles.composition_characteristics: Deep empty spaces, low horizon, scale contrast.
use_cases: conceptual frame ads (giant glasses in landscape)
styles.time_optic_fit: Strong for conceptual product ads (eye/vision metaphors, giant lenses showing a sharp world); avoid copying famous melting clocks or apple-face images.
styles.prompt_template: Surrealist painting of {subject} in {setting}, dreamlike impossible juxtaposition rendered with precise realism, long raking shadows, eerie stillness, {palette}, {lighting}, {composition}, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Surrealist painting of a giant pair of round glasses standing upright in a calm desert, the lenses showing a sharp green forest while the world around is blurred, precise realism, long raking evening shadows, eerie stillness, sand, sky blue and deep green palette, low horizon with the glasses centred, no text.
avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
styles.flux_notes: FLUX handles conceptual scenes well; lens contents often don't match the brief — use HTML compositing for the 'sharp through lens' effect.

styles.name: Pop Art
styles.name_th: ป๊อปอาร์ต
styles.historical_background: Pop art emerged in the mid-1950s in Britain and the late 1950s in America and peaked in the 1960s, drawing imagery from popular and commercial culture — films, advertising, packaging, music, comics; American pop used recognisable imagery with hard edges (Tate, 'Pop art').
styles.visual_characteristics: Bright flat colours, bold outlines, Ben-Day/halftone dots, repeated commercial icons.
styles.line_characteristics: Thick black outlines.
styles.shape_language: Iconic, simplified consumer objects and faces.
styles.color_characteristics: Primary and fluorescent brights, high contrast.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Flat, graphic.
styles.texture_characteristics: Printed dots, screenprint layers.
styles.composition_characteristics: Central icon, grids of repetition.
styles.time_optic_fit: Good for playful frame-grid posts (same frame in 4 colourways); loud — balance with brand neutrals.
common_mistakes: copying famous pop works or celebrities
styles.prompt_template: Pop art image of {subject}, bold black outlines, flat bright colours, halftone dot shading in select areas, {palette}, {composition}, repeated icon layout, no text, no celebrities.
styles.prompt_example: Pop art image of the same pair of cat-eye sunglasses repeated in a four-panel grid, each panel a different flat colour background, bold black outlines, halftone dot shading only on the lenses, peach, deep green, pink and sky blue, flatlay grid composition, no text, no celebrities.
avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
styles.flux_notes: Works but adds speech bubbles and fake words; negate. Better to repeat one real cutout in HTML with colour panels.

styles.name: Op Art
styles.name_th: อ็อปอาร์ต
styles.historical_background: Op art was a major 1960s painting movement using geometric forms to create optical effects based on colour theory and the psychology of perception, ranging from subtle to disorienting; Vasarely was among its originators (Tate, 'Op art').
styles.visual_characteristics: Precise repeated geometric patterns that appear to move, bulge or vibrate.
styles.line_characteristics: Crisp parallel lines, concentric rings, warped grids.
styles.color_characteristics: Black and white or high-contrast complementary pairs.
styles.lighting_characteristics: None; illusion from pattern.
styles.texture_characteristics: Flat hard-edge paint.
styles.composition_characteristics: All-over patterns with a distortion zone.
styles.time_optic_fit: Topical for an optical shop (optical illusions), but strong patterns can cause discomfort and moiré on phone screens; use subtly and never for eye-break content.
styles.prompt_template: Op art pattern of {subject}, precise black and white geometric lines warping to create an illusion of {setting}, hard-edged flat paint, {composition}, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Op art pattern of concentric circles that subtly bulge outward like a lens magnifying the centre, precise black and white geometric lines with a deep green accent ring, hard-edged flat paint, centred radial composition, no text.
avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
styles.flux_notes: FLUX geometry is imprecise; generate op patterns with code (SVG/canvas) instead.

styles.name: Minimalism
styles.name_th: มินิมอลลิสม์
styles.historical_background: Minimalism emerged in the late 1950s in the USA and flourished in the 1960s–70s; Frank Stella's Black Paintings were shown at MoMA in 1959; works use simple geometric forms, make no attempt to depict outside reality, and drew on Russian constructivist and suprematist ideas (Tate, 'Minimalism').
styles.visual_characteristics: Very few elements, large empty fields, precise geometry, restrained palette.
styles.line_characteristics: Clean straight edges or none.
styles.color_characteristics: Monochrome or two-colour; neutral or one saturated field.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Even soft; in photography, gentle gradient.
styles.texture_characteristics: Smooth, matte.
styles.composition_characteristics: Negative space dominant; centred or strict grid.
styles.time_optic_fit: Excellent: matches brand tokens (Snow, Timberwolf, Phthalo) and lets a single frame photo breathe.
styles.prompt_template: Minimalist composition of {subject} in {setting}, very few elements, large calm empty field, precise clean edges, {palette} in two or three tones, {lighting}, {composition}, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Minimalist composition for a single pair of glasses, a smooth timberwolf-coloured backdrop with one soft phthalo-green rectangle block as a plinth on the lower third, large calm empty field, precise clean edges, soft even light with a gentle gradient, centred placement for a product cutout, no text.
avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
styles.flux_notes: FLUX is good at minimalist backdrops; tends to add props — say 'nothing else in frame'.

styles.name: Abstract Expressionism
styles.name_th: แอบสแตรกต์เอ็กซ์เพรสชันนิสม์
styles.historical_background: Abstract expressionism emerged in the 1940s–50s among New York painters (the New York school), in two tendencies: action painting with sweeping gestural marks and colour field painting with large areas of single colour, drawing on surrealist automatism (Tate, 'Abstract expressionism').
styles.visual_characteristics: Large gestural marks, drips and splatters, or vast soft-edged colour fields.
styles.line_characteristics: Energetic gestural strokes, drips; or none in colour field.
styles.shape_language: Non-representational; organic gestures or soft rectangles.
styles.color_characteristics: Bold contrasts (action) or deep resonant fields (colour field).
styles.lighting_characteristics: Not depicted.
styles.texture_characteristics: Thick paint, drips, raw canvas stains.
styles.composition_characteristics: All-over or large stacked fields.
styles.time_optic_fit: Colour-field version makes calm premium backgrounds in brand colours; action-painting version suits bold launches. Never for informative content.
styles.prompt_template: Abstract expressionist painting, {subject}, {palette}, large gestural brushstrokes and drips OR soft-edged stacked colour fields, raw canvas texture, {composition}, non-representational, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Abstract expressionist colour field painting as a product backdrop, two soft-edged stacked fields of deep phthalo green over warm timberwolf with a thin glowing peach band between them, thin stained paint on raw canvas texture, horizontal stacked composition with the band on the lower third, non-representational, no text.
avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
styles.flux_notes: Colour fields are easy; gestural work can look like generic splatter. Untested in project.

styles.name: Ukiyo-e Woodblock
styles.name_th: ภาพพิมพ์แกะไม้อุกิโยเอะ
styles.historical_background: Ukiyo-e, 'pictures of the floating world', depicted the entertainment districts of Edo-period Japan (the V&A dates the period 1615–1868); in 1765 multi-block printing was perfected, producing full-colour nishiki-e ('brocade pictures'), each colour carved on its own block and aligned with registration marks, made by publisher, designer, block cutter and printer (V&A). Tate notes ukiyo-e were printed by hand pressure rather than a press (Tate, 'Woodcut').
styles.visual_characteristics: Flat areas of colour, elegant key-block outlines, patterned textiles, stylised waves and clouds, flattened space.
styles.line_characteristics: Fine, confident black key-block line with graceful taper.
styles.color_characteristics: Soft natural-pigment tones (indigo/Prussian blue, vermilion, soft yellows) with gradient wiping in skies.
styles.lighting_characteristics: No cast shadows; flat decorative light.
styles.texture_characteristics: Washi paper fibre, embossing, woodgrain in flat areas.
styles.composition_characteristics: Asymmetric, high or tilted viewpoints, dramatic cropping, foreground framing elements.
styles.time_optic_fit: Use respectfully as technique (flat colour, key line, gradient sky) for travel or rain-season content; avoid fake Japanese text/seals and imitations of famous prints (great wave).
styles.prompt_template: Japanese woodblock print technique depicting {subject} in {setting}, fine black key-block outlines, flat areas of colour, soft gradient-wiped sky, washi paper texture with slight woodgrain, {palette}, {composition} with dramatic cropping, no text, no seals, no cartouches.
styles.prompt_example: Japanese woodblock print technique depicting a person with an umbrella and round glasses crossing a small bridge in summer rain, fine black key-block outlines, flat areas of colour, rain as fine diagonal lines, soft gradient-wiped grey-blue sky, washi paper texture with slight woodgrain, indigo, deep green and soft peach, high viewpoint with the bridge cutting diagonally, no text, no seals, no cartouches.
avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
styles.flux_notes: FLUX knows the look well but almost always adds pseudo-kanji cartouches and the wave cliché; negate both.

styles.name: Thai Traditional Mural
styles.name_th: จิตรกรรมฝาผนังไทย
styles.historical_background: Siamese Buddhist murals in temples and palaces were standardised in the Rattanakosin (Bangkok) period after eighteenth-century experimentation, with marked change under King Rama III (c.1824–51); main subjects are Jataka tales of the Buddha's past lives, Traiphum cosmology and the Ramakien, arranged in bays between windows and divided by zig-zag sinthao lines (Royal Thai Embassy Seoul article). Recent scholarship analyses the oblique (diagonal) structure of early Rattanakosin compositions (Thai journal abstract).
styles.visual_characteristics: Continuous narrative scenes, flat figures in elegant gestures, pavilions and landscapes viewed obliquely, zig-zag dividers, gold accents.
styles.line_characteristics: Fine fluid contour lines defining figures, flame-like (kranok) ornament.
styles.shape_language: Stylised graceful figures; ornamented architecture; rocks and trees as patterns.
styles.color_characteristics: Earthy mineral reds, ochres, greens, dark backgrounds with gold leaf highlights (colour terms are general observation; the opened source does not detail pigments).
styles.lighting_characteristics: No cast shadows; flat even light.
styles.texture_characteristics: Aged wall plaster, fine cracks, gold leaf sheen.
styles.composition_characteristics: Many scenes on one wall, oblique bird's-eye layout, sinthao zig-zag separators, registers.
use_cases: Songkran/cultural greetings using secular village-life motifs only
story clips set in old Thailand with secular scenes
styles.time_optic_fit: Handle with care. Temple murals are sacred Buddhist art: never put the Buddha, monks, deities or Jataka scenes in a sales ad, never put glasses on sacred figures. Acceptable: secular village/market scenes, ornament-inspired borders, educational posts crediting the tradition. Prefer consulting the user before using it for promotion.
common_mistakes: using Buddha or sacred figures as decoration in ads
putting sunglasses on deities or monks
styles.prompt_template: Painting in the manner of a traditional Thai mural (secular scene) of {subject} in {setting}, flat figures with fine fluid contours, elegant stylised gestures, oblique bird's-eye arrangement with zig-zag dividing lines, earthy reds, ochres and greens with small gold accents ({palette}), flat even light, {composition}, aged plaster texture, no religious figures, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Painting in the manner of a traditional Thai mural (secular scene) of a lively riverside floating market with villagers trading fruit from boats, flat figures with fine fluid contours, elegant stylised gestures, oblique bird's-eye arrangement with zig-zag dividing lines, earthy reds, ochres and deep greens with small gold accents, flat even light, several small scenes across a wide panel, aged plaster texture, no religious figures, no text.
avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
styles.flux_notes: FLUX tends to produce generic 'Asian temple' art mixing Indian/Khmer elements and Buddha figures; check carefully and reject sacred content. Untested in project.

styles.name: Chinese Gongbi
styles.name_th: ภาพจีนกงปี่ (เขียนละเอียด)
styles.historical_background: Gongbi is a Chinese painting style of meticulous brushwork and highly coloured palettes, often on silk (V&A, 'Chinese gongbi silk painting', which shows a recreation but gives no technical history). styles.line_characteristics: Thin, even, controlled 'iron-wire'-like contour lines.
styles.color_characteristics: Mineral and plant colours built in many thin layers; soft gradations within outlines.
styles.lighting_characteristics: No cast shadows; even light.
styles.texture_characteristics: Silk weave or fine paper; aged tone.
styles.composition_characteristics: Asymmetric, open background, branch entering from edge.
use_cases: Chinese New Year posts (respectful, decorative flowers/birds)

styles.name: Persian Miniature
styles.name_th: จิตรกรรมจิ๋วเปอร์เซีย

styles.name: Folk / Naïve Art
styles.name_th: ศิลปะพื้นบ้าน/ไร้เดียงสา
styles.historical_background: Naïve art is simple work typically by makers without academy training, valued for its 'childlike simplicity of execution and vision'; Tate's examples include Henri Rousseau (c.1909–10), Alfred Wallis (c.1935–6) and André Bauchant (1940) (Tate, 'Naïve art'). Folk traditions worldwide share flat decorative qualities.
styles.visual_characteristics: Flat perspective, bright colours, repetitive patterns, figures and animals in frontal poses.
styles.line_characteristics: Simple outlines, hand-wobble.
styles.color_characteristics: Bright local colour, little shading.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Even, no cast shadows.
styles.texture_characteristics: Painted wood, board, canvas grain.
styles.composition_characteristics: Everything shown clearly; inconsistent scale by importance.
styles.time_optic_fit: Good for warm neighbourhood-shop community content (local market, festival); avoid appropriating a specific ethnic group's sacred patterns.

styles.name: Vintage Comic Halftone
styles.name_th: คอมิกวินเทจฮาล์ฟโทน

styles.color_characteristics: Limited CMYK, dot tints, primary-heavy.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Graphic shadows as black shapes.
styles.texture_characteristics: Paper yellowing, dot patterns, slight ink bleed.
styles.composition_characteristics: Panels, dramatic angles, speech-balloon space (text in HTML).

styles.name: Black-and-White Manga Screentone
styles.name_th: มังงะขาวดำสกรีนโทน
styles.historical_background: Japanese black-and-white comics use pen inking with adhesive (now digital) screentone sheets for grey values; the conventions (speed lines, tone gradients, expressive panelling) are discussed in comics theory such as McCloud (1993). No museum page opened; described as craft.
styles.visual_characteristics: Crisp pen lines, dot and gradient screentones, speed lines, expressive eyes, dramatic panelling.
styles.line_characteristics: Tapered G-pen lines, fine hatching, varied weight.
styles.shape_language: Stylised characters, large expressive eyes, dynamic poses.
styles.color_characteristics: Black, white and screentone greys only.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Tone gradients and spot blacks; sparkle effects.
styles.texture_characteristics: Dot screens, gradient tones, white-out highlights.
styles.composition_characteristics: Multi-panel pages, close-ups for emotion, speed-line focus.
styles.time_optic_fit: Good for comedic or emotional carousel stories (fogged glasses on noodles, first contact lens). Text must be English in HTML.
common_mistakes: muddy grey instead of screentone dots
styles.prompt_template: Black and white manga panel of {subject} in {setting}, crisp tapered pen lines, dot and gradient screentones, speed lines, spot blacks, expressive character, {composition}, no colour, no text, no sound effects lettering.
styles.prompt_example: Black and white manga panel of a young woman whose glasses fog up as she leans over a steaming bowl of noodles, crisp tapered pen lines, dot and gradient screentones, radial speed lines, spot blacks, comedic exaggerated expression, close-up on her face with the bowl in the foreground, no colour, no text, no sound effects lettering.
avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
styles.flux_notes: FLUX makes convincing manga panels but adds Japanese SFX lettering; negate; screentone sometimes becomes grey wash.

styles.name: Anime Cel Shading
styles.name_th: อนิเมะแบบเซล
styles.historical_background: Cel animation painted characters on transparent celluloid over painted backgrounds; Japanese TV anime developed a two-tone shading convention (base colour plus one hard shadow, sometimes a highlight). Described as craft; no museum source opened.
styles.visual_characteristics: Clean line art, flat base colours with one hard-edged shadow tone, simple highlights, detailed painted background.
styles.line_characteristics: Thin, even, clean outlines.
styles.shape_language: Stylised characters with large eyes, simplified noses, expressive hair shapes.
styles.color_characteristics: Flat bright fills, coloured shadows (cool), consistent character model colours.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Two-tone hard shading, rim lights, lens flares sparingly.
styles.texture_characteristics: Smooth, no texture on characters; painterly backgrounds.
styles.composition_characteristics: Cinematic framing, character over detailed background, clear silhouettes.
styles.time_optic_fit: Good for story clips and youth content; character consistency across frames needs reference sheets. Avoid imitating known studios.
common_mistakes: glasses drawn without lenses or merged into face
styles.prompt_template: Anime cel-shaded illustration of {subject} in {setting}, clean thin line art, flat base colours with one hard-edged shadow tone, simple highlights, {palette}, {lighting}, {composition}, detailed painted background, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Anime cel-shaded illustration of a teenage boy pushing up his new rectangular glasses with a confident smile in a sunny school corridor, clean thin line art, flat base colours with one hard-edged cool shadow tone, simple lens highlights, deep green blazer, warm skin tones and soft blue sky, afternoon window light with rim light, medium shot on the left third with corridor perspective, detailed painted background, no text.
avoid_phrases: in the style of <any living artist>
styles.flux_notes: FLUX does clean anime cels reasonably; glasses frames often lose one side or lenses vanish — inspect and inpaint; consistency needs seed/img2img.

styles.name: Anime painterly background
styles.name_th: ฉากหลังอนิเมะแบบวาดสี
styles.historical_background: Hand-painted backgrounds for Japanese TV and film animation were traditionally made in opaque poster colour on paper and photographed under cels; since the 2000s most are painted digitally while keeping the brushy, opaque look. (Artistic overview; no history page opened.)
styles.visual_characteristics: Detailed, lush environments behind simpler cel characters: towering cumulus skies, sunlit streets, overgrown greenery, glowing windows.
styles.line_characteristics: Almost no outlines in the background; edges are painted, crisp on architecture and soft on foliage and clouds.
styles.shape_language: Big readable masses (sky, hill, building) broken into many small leaf and cloud clusters; perspective-correct man-made forms.
styles.color_characteristics: Saturated but natural: deep cerulean skies, warm cream highlights, cool blue-violet shadows; strong warm/cool temperature shifts.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Clear sun direction, bright rim on clouds, soft bounce, light shafts and lens bloom; time of day drives the whole palette.
styles.texture_characteristics: Gouache-like opaque strokes, soft gradients in sky, small dry-brush flecks on foliage; no grain or photo texture.
styles.composition_characteristics: Wide establishing shots, low horizon to show sky, strong leading lines of streets or rails, room left for a character.
styles.emotional_characteristics: Nostalgic, hopeful, summery, quietly lonely or wonder-filled.
styles.time_optic_fit: Good for story-clip backdrops (e.g. the shop street at dusk) and calm carousel backgrounds; never for the product itself. A real frame cutout can sit on such a background only if lighting direction is matched.
common_mistakes: characters rendered in the same painterly detail so they sink into the background
over-saturated sky that kills the subject
styles.prompt_template: Hand-painted animation background of {subject} in {setting}, opaque gouache-like brushwork, crisp painted architecture, soft clustered foliage, towering clouds, {palette}, {lighting}, {composition}, no characters unless stated, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Hand-painted animation background of a small corner eyewear shop with a glowing window in a narrow Bangkok soi, opaque gouache-like brushwork, crisp painted shutters, soft clustered potted plants, towering pink clouds, warm cream and cerulean with Phthalo green shop sign shape (no letters), golden hour light from the left, low horizon with leading lines of the street, no characters, no text.
avoid_phrases: titles of copyrighted films, games or series
styles.flux_notes: FLUX schnell produces convincing painterly skies and streets; it tends to add stray signage text (say 'no text, blank signs') and sometimes adds characters.

styles.name: Chibi / kawaii
styles.name_th: ชิบิ / คาวาอี้
styles.historical_background: Kawaii ('cute') aesthetics became a mainstream Japanese visual culture from the 1970s onward, and 'chibi' super-deformed proportions (very large head, tiny body) became a standard comic and merchandise convention. (Artistic overview; no history page opened.)
styles.visual_characteristics: Characters 2–3 heads tall, oversized heads and eyes, tiny hands and feet, rosy cheeks, simple expressions; props shrunk to toy-like scale.
styles.line_characteristics: Clean rounded outlines of even or gently tapered weight, often slightly thicker outer contour.
styles.shape_language: Circles and soft rounded rectangles; no sharp angles; bean-shaped bodies.
styles.color_characteristics: Pastels and candy colours with a few saturated accents; white highlights in eyes; pink blush.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Flat or one-step cel shading, soft glow, sparkle effects.
styles.texture_characteristics: Smooth flat fills, sometimes subtle paper or soft airbrush gradient.
styles.composition_characteristics: Centered single character or a tight cluster, generous negative space, stickers and icons around.
styles.time_optic_fit: Fits kids' frames and playful tips (e.g. 'clean your lenses'); a chibi character can wear a simplified frame icon, but real product shots must stay the real photo next to it.
common_mistakes: adult proportions with just big eyes
hands with five detailed fingers drawn badly
drawing a real frame model in chibi form and implying it is the product
styles.prompt_template: Cute chibi character of {subject}, 2.5 heads tall, oversized head and eyes, tiny hands, rounded clean outlines, flat cel colour with soft blush, {setting}, {palette}, {lighting}, {composition}, plain background, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Cute chibi optometrist girl holding a giant pair of round glasses, 2.5 heads tall, oversized head and sparkly eyes, tiny hands, rounded clean outlines, flat cel colour with soft blush, standing in a tiny toy-like shop, pastel peach and snow with Phthalo green accent, soft even light, centered with negative space, plain background, no text.
avoid_phrases: titles of copyrighted films, games or series
styles.flux_notes: FLUX handles chibi proportions well; it tends toward glossy 3D-looking shading unless 'flat cel colour, 2D' is stated.

styles.name: Rubber-hose cartoon (1920s–30s)
styles.name_th: การ์ตูนแขนสายยาง ยุค 1920–30
styles.historical_background: Rubber-hose animation was the dominant style of American cartoons of the 1920s and early 1930s: bendy, boneless limbs, pie-cut eyes, white gloves; it is credited to animator Bill Nolan in silent-era shorts and faded by the mid-1930s as studios moved to more realistic movement (Cartoon Brew).
styles.visual_characteristics: Bouncy black-and-white (or limited colour) characters with noodle arms, round bodies, pie-cut eyes, white gloves and big shoes; everything squashes and stretches.
styles.line_characteristics: Bold, smooth ink lines of fairly even weight; limbs drawn as single flowing curves with no elbows or knees.
styles.shape_language: Circles and tubes; bodies like balls or pears; props alive with faces.
styles.color_characteristics: Black, white and greys, or faded early two-strip-like colour (muted red, teal, cream); aged-film feel.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Flat lighting, small drop shadows under feet, no modelled shading.
styles.texture_characteristics: Film grain, gate weave, slight vignette, paper-cel flatness.
styles.composition_characteristics: Stage-like side view, characters centred, simple repeating backgrounds, iris-in/out framing.
styles.time_optic_fit: Good for a retro mascot or gag about lost glasses; keep product out of the cartoon or place the real cutout beside it. Strongly vintage, so use sparingly.
common_mistakes: too-clean digital lines with no film texture
styles.prompt_template: 1920s–30s rubber-hose cartoon of {subject}, boneless noodle limbs, pie-cut eyes, white gloves, bold even ink lines, {setting}, {palette}, {lighting}, {composition}, film grain and slight vignette, no text.
styles.prompt_example: 1920s–30s rubber-hose cartoon of a cheerful pair of glasses with tiny noodle legs dancing on a shop counter, boneless limbs, pie-cut eyes, white gloves, bold even ink lines, simple shop backdrop, black white and warm cream, flat light with drop shadow, centered stage view with iris vignette, film grain, no text.
avoid_phrases: titles of copyrighted films, games or series
styles.flux_notes: FLUX gets the look roughly but often adds modern shading or invents known mascots; name traits (pie-cut eyes, noodle limbs) rather than eras alone.

styles.name: Modern TV cartoon
styles.name_th: การ์ตูนทีวียุคใหม่
styles.historical_background: Contemporary TV animation (roughly 2000s onward) favours flat colour, thick simple outlines and graphic shapes designed for fast digital (vector/puppet) production. (Artistic overview; no history page opened.)
styles.visual_characteristics: Simplified characters with geometric heads, dot or bean eyes, flat colour, expressive poses; clean flat backgrounds.
styles.line_characteristics: Uniform or slightly varying outlines, often coloured lines; very few interior lines.
styles.shape_language: Strong geometric shapes: squares for stubborn characters, circles for friendly, triangles for villains.
styles.color_characteristics: Bright flat palette, limited per scene, one shadow tone per colour.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Flat lighting or a single hard cel shadow; occasional rim for drama.
styles.texture_characteristics: Clean vector fills, optional subtle grain overlay.
styles.composition_characteristics: Clear staging, characters mid-shot, background simplified to support silhouette readability.
use_cases: ร้านแว่นตีสอง story clips
styles.time_optic_fit: Very good fit for the 16:9 story clips and rig.js puppets; product appears as a simplified prop in the story, and as a real photo only in a separate end card.
styles.prompt_template: Modern flat TV cartoon of {subject}, geometric character design, simple dot eyes, flat colours with one cel shadow, clean outlines, {setting}, {palette}, {lighting}, {composition}, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Modern flat TV cartoon of a sleepy shop owner at 2 a.m. polishing a lens behind the counter, geometric character design, simple dot eyes, flat colours with one cel shadow, clean outlines, small eyewear shop interior with display shelves, Phthalo green and Raisin black with peach lamp glow, practical lamp light, medium shot rule of thirds, no text.
avoid_phrases: titles of copyrighted films, games or series
styles.flux_notes: FLUX does clean flat cartoons well; keep prompts short and state 'flat 2D vector'. Character consistency across shots is poor — use rig puppets for continuity.

styles.name: Webtoon digital comic
styles.name_th: เว็บตูน
styles.historical_background: Vertical-scroll digital comics developed on Korean web portals in the 2000s and spread globally via mobile apps; the format replaced the page with a long strip read by scrolling. (Artistic overview; no history page opened.)
styles.visual_characteristics: Full-colour digital panels stacked vertically, soft-shaded attractive characters, lots of space between panels, speech bubbles.
styles.line_characteristics: Clean thin digital lines, slightly tapered; lighter line than print manga.
styles.shape_language: Elongated, stylish proportions; rounded faces; simple background shapes or blurred photo-like backgrounds.
styles.color_characteristics: Soft colour with airbrush gradients, glow overlays, pastel or moody filters per scene.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Soft cel shading plus overlay glow, coloured rim light, bloom.
styles.texture_characteristics: Smooth digital, gradient overlays, occasional texture brushes.
styles.composition_characteristics: Vertical flow, one beat per panel, white gutters as pacing, close-ups for emotion.
styles.time_optic_fit: Good for vertical story Reels and carousels; panels can include a simplified frame, the real product only in a final photo panel.
common_mistakes: horizontal page layouts in a vertical format
styles.prompt_template: Vertical webtoon panel of {subject}, clean thin digital lines, soft cel shading with airbrush gradients and gentle glow, {setting}, {palette}, {lighting}, {composition}, empty speech area, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Vertical webtoon panel of a young woman trying on round glasses in a mirror and smiling shyly, clean thin digital lines, soft cel shading with airbrush gradients and gentle glow, bright eyewear shop with wooden shelves, snow and timberwolf with peach accents, soft window light, close-up over the shoulder into the mirror, empty speech area at top, no text.
avoid_phrases: titles of copyrighted films, games or series
styles.flux_notes: FLUX makes attractive webtoon-like faces; it often adds bubble text — keep bubbles out and add them in HTML.

styles.name: Graphic-novel noir
styles.name_th: นิยายภาพแนวนัวร์
styles.historical_background: Noir comics adapt the hard-boiled crime fiction and 1940s film noir look: heavy black spotting, stark contrast and limited colour. (Artistic overview; comics grammar per McCloud1993, bibliographic.)
styles.visual_characteristics: High-contrast ink drawings dominated by solid blacks, rain, cigarette smoke, slatted shadows, hard faces.
styles.line_characteristics: Heavy brush inks, bold silhouettes, little hatching; shapes defined by black masses rather than lines.
styles.shape_language: Angular, sharp shapes; tall verticals of buildings; harsh triangles of light.
styles.color_characteristics: Black and white, sometimes one spot colour (red, yellow, or brand green).
styles.lighting_characteristics: Hard single sources, venetian-blind shadows, streetlights, underlight; deep cast shadows.
styles.texture_characteristics: Flat ink, occasional splatter or dry brush; no gradients.
styles.composition_characteristics: Dramatic angles, tilted frames, tight close-ups, silhouettes in doorways.
styles.time_optic_fit: Good for a mystery/drama episode or a teaser ('who stole the glasses?'); one brand-green spot colour ties it to Time Optic. Not for product ads.
common_mistakes: grey mush instead of solid blacks
styles.prompt_template: Graphic-novel noir panel of {subject}, heavy brush ink, solid black masses, stark white highlights, {setting}, black and white with one spot colour {palette}, {lighting}, {composition}, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Graphic-novel noir panel of a detective holding up a pair of glasses under a streetlight, heavy brush ink, solid black masses, stark white highlights, rainy alley beside a closed shop, black and white with one spot colour Phthalo green on the glasses, venetian-blind hard light, low-angle diagonal composition, no text.
avoid_phrases: titles of copyrighted films, games or series
styles.flux_notes: FLUX does high-contrast ink fairly well; spot colour often leaks into other areas. Untested at scale here.

styles.name: Editorial conceptual illustration
styles.name_th: ภาพประกอบเชิงแนวคิด (บทบรรณาธิการ)
styles.historical_background: Conceptual editorial illustration, common in magazines and newspapers, communicates an idea through visual metaphor rather than literal depiction. (Artistic overview; no history page opened.)
styles.visual_characteristics: A single clever visual metaphor: glasses as windows, lenses as moons, a head opening like a drawer; simplified figures and objects.
styles.line_characteristics: Clean or slightly textured lines; often no lines, just shapes.
styles.shape_language: Simplified geometric shapes, surreal scale shifts, visual puns.
styles.color_characteristics: Limited palette of 3–5 colours, bold contrast between metaphor and ground.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Flat or soft graphic shading; light used symbolically.
styles.texture_characteristics: Grainy riso-like or brush textures over flat shapes.
styles.composition_characteristics: Strong central idea, lots of negative space, room for a headline.
styles.time_optic_fit: Excellent for eye-health topics (blue light, myopia, UV) as metaphors; product stays out or as real photo on another slide.
styles.prompt_template: Conceptual editorial illustration showing {subject} as a visual metaphor, simplified shapes, limited palette {palette}, textured flat colour, {setting}, {lighting}, {composition}, generous negative space for a headline, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Conceptual editorial illustration showing a child's eye as a tiny window looking out at a vast screen-lit city, simplified shapes, limited palette Phthalo green, peach and snow, textured flat colour, minimal room, soft graphic light, centered with generous negative space for a headline, no text.
avoid_phrases: titles of copyrighted films, games or series
styles.flux_notes: FLUX can make metaphors if they are described concretely (objects + relationship); abstract instructions like 'visual metaphor for X' alone give generic results.

styles.name: Children's book crayon
styles.name_th: ภาพหนังสือเด็กสีเทียน
styles.historical_background: Wax crayon and oil pastel have long been used in picture books for their childlike, tactile mark-making. (Artistic overview; no history page opened.)
styles.visual_characteristics: Naive, joyful drawings with waxy strokes, visible paper tooth, simple figures and big suns.
styles.line_characteristics: Wobbly, uneven crayon lines with broken edges where the paper grain shows.
styles.shape_language: Simple, chunky, slightly lopsided shapes; childlike proportions.
styles.color_characteristics: Bright primaries and secondaries, layered waxy colour with white paper showing through.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Implied light only; flat colour, maybe a scribbled sun.
styles.texture_characteristics: Heavy waxy grain, scribble fills, sgraffito scratches.
styles.composition_characteristics: Simple horizon, big central subject, playful scattered elements.
styles.time_optic_fit: Good for children's eye-test or kids' frames campaigns; real kids' frame photo shown separately or as a cutout on the crayon page.
styles.prompt_template: Children's picture book illustration of {subject} in wax crayon, wobbly uneven lines, scribble fills with paper grain showing, chunky simple shapes, {setting}, {palette}, {lighting}, {composition}, white paper background, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Children's picture book illustration of a small boy reading the eye chart at an eye test in wax crayon, wobbly uneven lines, scribble fills with paper grain showing, chunky simple shapes, cheerful shop room, bright primaries with green, implied soft light, centered subject, white paper background, no text.
avoid_phrases: titles of copyrighted films, games or series
styles.flux_notes: FLUX imitates crayon texture reasonably; tends to make it too neat — add 'drawn by a child-like hand, uneven'.

styles.name: Minimal line art
styles.name_th: ลายเส้นมินิมอล
styles.historical_background: Minimal line drawing descends from contour drawing traditions; in modern branding it is used for clean, elegant spot illustrations. (Artistic overview.)
styles.visual_characteristics: Sparse single-weight lines describing people, objects or faces with lots of white space; may have one flat colour shape behind.
styles.line_characteristics: Thin, uniform, confident lines; few strokes; open contours.
styles.shape_language: Simplified, elegant shapes; implied rather than closed forms.
styles.color_characteristics: Monochrome line on light ground, optional single accent blob.
styles.lighting_characteristics: None; form implied by line.
styles.texture_characteristics: Clean vector or fine pen on smooth paper.
styles.composition_characteristics: Lots of negative space; subject small or centred.
styles.time_optic_fit: Core house style: brand/store-lineart.png and the dialogue carousels already use it. Simple glasses shapes may be drawn, but never presented as a specific stocked model.
styles.prompt_template: Minimal line art of {subject}, thin uniform single-weight black line, few strokes, open contours, {setting}, lots of white space, {palette}, {composition}, no shading, lighting: {lighting}, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Minimal line art of two faceless figures sitting at a café table, one adjusting her glasses, thin uniform single-weight black line, few strokes, open contours, implied table only, lots of white space, raisin line on snow with one peach circle behind, centered with negative space, no shading, no text.
avoid_phrases: titles of copyrighted films, games or series
styles.flux_notes: FLUX does clean line art well; sometimes adds grey shading or a texture — say 'pure line, no shading'.

styles.name: Continuous one-line drawing
styles.name_th: ภาพลายเส้นเดียวต่อเนื่อง
styles.historical_background: Continuous-line drawing, where the pen never lifts, is a long-standing drawing exercise and decorative style widely used in modern branding. (Artistic overview.)
styles.visual_characteristics: A single unbroken line looping into faces, hands, glasses or objects.
styles.line_characteristics: One continuous stroke of even weight, loops and overlaps visible.
styles.color_characteristics: One line colour on a plain ground, sometimes a soft colour shape.
styles.lighting_characteristics: None.
styles.texture_characteristics: Clean vector or ink.
styles.composition_characteristics: Centred or offset with large negative space.
styles.time_optic_fit: Good as decorative art (a face wearing glasses in one line). A one-line glasses shape is fine as an icon, not as product depiction.
styles.prompt_template: Continuous one-line drawing of {subject}, single unbroken even line with visible loops, {setting} implied, {palette}, {composition}, plain background, lighting: {lighting}, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Continuous one-line drawing of a woman's profile wearing cat-eye glasses, single unbroken even line with visible loops, no setting, Phthalo green line on snow with soft peach shape, offset left with negative space, plain background, no text.
avoid_phrases: titles of copyrighted films, games or series
styles.flux_notes: FLUX often breaks the line into several strokes; results look 'one-line style' rather than truly continuous. Vector-trace if exactness matters.

styles.name: Sketchnote doodle
styles.name_th: สเก็ตช์โน้ต / ดูเดิล
styles.historical_background: Sketchnoting — visual note-taking mixing drawings, arrows and lettering — became popular in the 2000s–2010s as a learning and meeting-capture method. (Artistic overview.)
styles.visual_characteristics: Hand-drawn icons, arrows, frames, banners and little characters arranged like notebook notes.
styles.line_characteristics: Marker lines of medium weight, slightly wobbly; arrows and containers.
styles.shape_language: Simple icons, speech bubbles, banners, boxes.
styles.color_characteristics: Black marker with 1–2 highlight colours (grey shadow, one accent).
styles.lighting_characteristics: Flat, sometimes grey marker drop shadow.
styles.texture_characteristics: Marker on paper, slight bleed.
styles.composition_characteristics: Structured: flow, arrows, numbered steps; grid or path layout.
styles.time_optic_fit: Good for tips like 'how to choose frames for your face shape' — draw icons only; letters must be added in HTML (Thai/English).
styles.prompt_template: Sketchnote doodle page about {subject}, hand-drawn marker icons, arrows, empty banners and boxes, slight wobble, black line with one accent {palette}, {composition}, {setting}, empty boxes for text, lighting: {lighting}, no letters.
styles.prompt_example: Sketchnote doodle page about caring for your glasses: icons of a microfiber cloth, a case, water drop and a sun, hand-drawn marker icons, arrows, empty banners and boxes, slight wobble, black line with one Phthalo green accent and grey shadow, z-pattern flow, plain paper, empty boxes for text, no letters.
avoid_phrases: titles of copyrighted films, games or series
styles.flux_notes: FLUX will add fake handwriting unless told 'no letters, empty boxes'; still check for scribble text.

styles.name: Technical blueprint
styles.name_th: แบบพิมพ์เขียว
styles.historical_background: Blueprints were produced by the cyanotype process (white lines on Prussian blue) from the 19th century until diazo prints and CAD replaced them; the look survives as a design shorthand for engineering. (Artistic overview; no history page opened.)
styles.visual_characteristics: White technical line drawings on blue: orthographic views, dimension lines, callouts, grid.
styles.line_characteristics: Thin precise ruled lines, dashed hidden lines, dimension arrows.
styles.color_characteristics: Prussian/cyan blue ground with white or pale cyan lines.
styles.lighting_characteristics: None.
styles.texture_characteristics: Slight paper fibre, faded print mottle.
styles.composition_characteristics: Multiple views on a grid, title block area, symmetric layouts.
styles.time_optic_fit: Strong for 'anatomy of a frame' or lens-coating explainers. If a specific stocked frame is shown, trace from its real photo (vector-trace), do not let the model invent parts.
common_mistakes: inaccurate hinge details claimed as real
styles.prompt_template: Technical blueprint drawing of {subject}, white precise ruled lines on Prussian blue, orthographic front and side views, dashed hidden lines, dimension arrows without numbers, faint grid, {composition}, {palette}, setting: {setting}, lighting: {lighting}, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Technical blueprint drawing of a generic round metal eyeglass frame, white precise ruled lines on Prussian blue, orthographic front and side views, dashed hidden lines, dimension arrows without numbers, faint grid, symmetric centered layout, Prussian blue and white, no text.
avoid_phrases: titles of copyrighted films, games or series
styles.flux_notes: FLUX makes convincing blueprint looks but invents unreadable labels; geometry is approximate.

styles.name: Scientific botanical illustration
styles.name_th: ภาพพฤกษศาสตร์เชิงวิทยาศาสตร์
styles.historical_background: Scientific botanical illustration grew from printed herbals and naturalists' plates of the early modern period, prioritising accurate identification (whole plant, dissected parts) over expression. (Artistic overview; Met essay on botanical imagery found but fetch failed, not read.)
styles.visual_characteristics: Precise plant specimens on white: stems, leaves, flowers, roots and dissected parts arranged as a plate.
styles.line_characteristics: Fine, accurate contour lines, stippling or hatching for form.
styles.color_characteristics: Naturalistic watercolour, subtle and true to specimen.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Even, soft light from upper left, minimal cast shadow.
styles.texture_characteristics: Smooth watercolour on hot-press paper, fine stipple.
styles.composition_characteristics: Plate layout, centred specimen, parts arranged around.
use_cases: natural-material frame stories (wood, acetate from cotton)
styles.time_optic_fit: Niche: nice for sustainability/natural acetate topics or as decorative borders. No product depiction.
styles.prompt_template: Scientific botanical illustration plate of {subject}, precise fine contour lines and stipple, naturalistic watercolour, specimen and dissected parts arranged on white, {lighting}, {palette}, {composition}, no labels, setting: {setting}, no text.
styles.prompt_example: Scientific botanical illustration plate of a cotton plant with open boll, seeds and leaf (the raw source of cellulose acetate), precise fine contour lines and stipple, naturalistic watercolour, arranged on white, soft light from upper left, natural greens and creams, centered plate layout, no labels, no text.
avoid_phrases: titles of copyrighted films, games or series
styles.flux_notes: FLUX produces attractive plates; botanical accuracy is not reliable — check against a real specimen if the topic is factual.

styles.name: Fashion illustration
styles.name_th: ภาพประกอบแฟชั่น
styles.historical_background: Fashion illustration, from early 20th-century fashion plates to magazine croquis, exaggerates elongated figures and gesture to sell attitude and garment. (Artistic overview.)
styles.visual_characteristics: Elongated figures (9+ heads), confident gestural strokes, garment and accessory emphasis, loose wash colour.
styles.line_characteristics: Expressive, tapered ink or marker lines, lost-and-found edges.
styles.shape_language: Long verticals, S-curve poses, angular stylish shapes.
styles.color_characteristics: Loose marker/watercolour wash, often limited palette with one bold accent.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Implied, minimal shading.
styles.texture_characteristics: Marker streaks, watercolour blooms, paper white.
styles.composition_characteristics: Full figure vertical, lots of white space.
styles.time_optic_fit: Good for 'which frame fits your style' carousels: draw outfit and attitude, show glasses as a simple accessory, place real frame photos beside. Never present an illustrated frame as a stocked model.
styles.prompt_template: Fashion illustration of {subject}, elongated figure, confident tapered ink strokes, loose marker and watercolour wash, {setting}, {palette}, {lighting}, {composition}, lots of white paper, no text.

styles.name: Pixel art
styles.name_th: พิกเซลอาร์ต
styles.historical_background: Pixel art grew from the hardware limits of 1970s–90s computers and consoles, where every pixel and palette entry was placed by hand; it is now a deliberate retro aesthetic. Tate dates 'digital art' as a term to the early 1980s.
styles.visual_characteristics: Low-resolution images built from visible square pixels, limited palette, crisp edges, dithering.
styles.line_characteristics: 1-pixel outlines (often coloured), no anti-aliasing.
styles.shape_language: Blocky simplified forms, readable silhouettes at small sizes.
styles.color_characteristics: Restricted palette (8–32 colours), hue-shifted ramps.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Stepped shading ramps, dithered gradients, pixel highlights.
styles.texture_characteristics: Dithering patterns, hard pixel grid.
styles.composition_characteristics: Game-like side view or top-down; tiles.
styles.time_optic_fit: Playful for 'level up your vision' style posts; real frames shown as photo in another slide.

styles.name: Low poly
styles.name_th: โลว์โพลี
styles.historical_background: Low-polygon modelling was a necessity of early real-time 3D graphics; since the 2010s it is used deliberately as a faceted, geometric aesthetic. (Artistic overview.)
styles.visual_characteristics: Objects and landscapes built from visible flat triangles, each facet one colour.
styles.line_characteristics: No outlines; facet edges form the lines.
styles.color_characteristics: Gradient across facets, often pastel or sunset ramps.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Flat-shaded facets catch a single directional light.
styles.texture_characteristics: Clean flat facets, no texture.
styles.composition_characteristics: Isolated objects or wide stylised landscapes.

styles.shape_language: Simplified big shapes with detail at focal point.
styles.color_characteristics: Rich, harmonious, temperature-shifted colour.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Strong value design, warm/cool light and shadow.
styles.texture_characteristics: Brush texture, canvas or chalk brushes.
styles.composition_characteristics: Classical focal hierarchy, value grouping.

styles.name: Matte painting
styles.name_th: แมตต์เพนติ้ง
styles.historical_background: Matte painting began as painted glass placed in front of the camera; Norman Dawn is credited as the first cinematographer to use glass shots, in 1907, to 'restore' crumbling mission buildings, later combining them with matte shots (American Cinematographer). Digital matte painting continues the practice.
styles.visual_characteristics: Photoreal wide environments extending a set or location; seamless blending of painting and photo.
styles.line_characteristics: No lines; photographic edges.
styles.color_characteristics: Natural, matched to plate photography.

styles.texture_characteristics: Photographic; painted detail hidden.
styles.composition_characteristics: Wide establishing shots, horizon extension.

styles.name_th: ไอโซเมตริก 3D
styles.historical_background: Isometric projection — parallel projection with equal axes — has a long history in technical drawing and became a common look in games and infographics. (Artistic overview.)

styles.line_characteristics: No outlines or thin edges; parallel lines never converge.
styles.color_characteristics: Bright, soft pastel or brand colours.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Soft global illumination, gentle shadows.
styles.texture_characteristics: Smooth matte surfaces.
styles.composition_characteristics: Isolated diorama centred on plain ground.

styles.name: Claymation
styles.name_th: เคลย์แอนิเมชัน
styles.historical_background: Clay animation is a form of stop-motion in which plasticine figures are re-posed by hand and photographed one frame at a time. Its charm comes from the visible handling marks that frame-by-frame sculpting leaves behind. (Artistic overview; no history page opened.)
styles.visual_characteristics: Plasticine characters and props with fingerprints, soft lumpy rounded forms, miniature hand-built sets, tiny real-world scale.
styles.line_characteristics: No drawn lines; edges are soft rounded clay with occasional sculpting-tool grooves.

styles.color_characteristics: Saturated but slightly chalky clay colours; matte surfaces; colour comes from the material, not paint gradients.
styles.lighting_characteristics: Miniature studio lighting: soft key with gentle fill, small hard shadows, shallow depth of field revealing miniature scale.
styles.texture_characteristics: Fingerprints, tool marks, slight dust and seams; matte, not glossy.
styles.composition_characteristics: Miniature sets shot close; macro-like depth of field; centred characters with simple backdrops.

clay copy of a real frame presented as the product
